🇮🇱 ⚠️ #Netanyahu Claims #Arab Parties Stole #Israel's Election, Demands Investigation After Arab Voter Gains, No Majority Deadlocked Results: 
Washington Examiner: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday said rival Arab parties cheated in his country’s elections after exit polls indicated his coalition failed to capture a majority in the #Knesset, pushing the Middle Eastern democracy into a political deadlock.
Netanyahu’s Likud party and its allies outperformed expectations on Tuesday. But with results still trickling in on Wednesday evening, the prime minister failed to keep his majority in the Israeli parliament. There is still no clear winner. The opposition bloc, led by Gadi #Eisenkot’s Yashar party, remains Likud’s top rival. But two Arab parties, the Joint List and Ra’am, outperformed as they gained seats, drawing historic support as they are to win their largest-ever share of the vote.
Before the election, Netanyahu’s coalition held around 68 of the 120 Knesset seats, and the main opposition to him held around 49 seats.
With roughly 89% of the vote counted Wednesday evening, Netanyahu’s bloc held 53 seats. The main opposition, led by Eisenkot’s Yashar bloc, held 48 seats.
No bloc reached the winning number of 61 lawmakers, the size of a Knesset coalition necessary to form a government. But Arab parties made the biggest gains, with 19 seats, up from the 10 held by the United Arab List and the Joint List before the elections.
Netanyahu said the Arab parties had stolen the election, claiming they are guilty of criminal offenses of bribery, threats, violence, forgeries, and the use of prohibited software to mobilize voters.
“This is a serious blow to Israeli democracy and the voting rights of Israeli citizens,” he said in a post to X. “The law enforcement agencies must act with an iron fist and in an immediate manner.”
Netanyahu demanded election authorities in Israel immediately investigate his allegations, promising that his Likud party would produce hundreds of testimonies and pieces of evidence regarding election theft in many Arab polling stations, including thousands of envelopes with cash and Ra’am slips, threats and violence against polling station members, multiple voting behind the curtain, voting with double identities, discrepancies between the number of envelopes and the number of voters, and the use of prohibited mobilization software."

🇨🇳 Is China fielding a heavier-punching Yitian-L defense system on its Humvee equivalent?
China’s Yitian-L short-range air defense system appears to have undergone an evolutionary upgrade, judging by images circulating online and cited in The Defence Blog. The Dongfeng Mengshi 4×4 is now speculated to carry two six-round missile packs, tripling ready-to-fire capacity from four to 12 missiles.
The reworked launcher replaces the earlier four separate canisters with two compact six-tube boxes. Whether the missiles remain standard TY-90s or a smaller derivative remains unclear.
Key facts on the baseline system:
🔴 lightweight version of the Yitian family, designed to protect troops and sites against low-flying helicopters, drones, and cruise missiles
🔴 standard load packs four TY-90 infrared-guided missiles plus a folding 3D X-band radar (detection up to 18 km, per NORINCO)
🔴 500 m–6 km estimated engagement range, up to 4 km altitude; fire-and-forget heat-seeking guidance that avoids continuous radar emission
🔴 two operators control system from inside the vehicle via a digital console
The US has a similar solution in its Avenger system, which mounts short-range Stinger missiles on a light tactical vehicle to provide mobile air defense against low-altitude threats. [It is currently being deployed to protect Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77045) and the nearby Palm Beach airport.

🇮🇱 Israel’s election deadlock: Three ways Netanyahu could still hold on to power
 
Israel’s election has left Benjamin Netanyahu without[ a parliamentary majority](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76989), but another confrontation with Iran could throw him a political lifeline, reports The Cradle.
[The 27 October Knesset vote](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77008) left neither side able to secure the 61 seats needed to govern.
 
Palestinian lawmakers with 19 seats - their strongest representation in Knesset history - could determine who forms the next government, yet most Zionist opposition parties refuse to rely on their support.
 
Possible routes out of the deadlock include:
 
Emergency unity government
🌏 renewed war with Iran could push Eisenkot into an alliance with Netanyahu under the banner of national security
🌏 arrangement could preserve Netanyahu as PM, potentially with a rotation agreement, bring opposition figures into government, sideline both Palestinian and ultra-Orthodox parties
 
Opposition minority government:
♦️ Eisenkot could attempt to replace Netanyahu with the backing of Palestinian lawmakers
♦️ his allies refuse to cooperate with Arab parties; Palestinian political forces remain divided over supporting a Zionist government
 
Another election:
🔴 if coalition negotiations collapse, Netanyahu could remain caretaker prime minister until another vote is held
 
Netanyahu has another reason to avoid losing power: his ongoing corruption trial and demands for a probe into the security failures preceding Operation Al-Aqsa Flood.
Furthermore, Israel reportedly fears that even though the US may strike Iran again, [it will not fight for Netanyahu’s maximalist goals](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77059) of regime change and total destruction of Iran’s nuclear program.

🇮🇱 Israel fears a short US campaign will leave it alone with a stronger Iran
The US may be willing to launch another round of strikes on Iran, but not to fight until Israel gets its coveted objective of regime change and the destruction of Iran's nuclear program, Haaretz reports.
👉 The central concern is reportedly a mismatch between US and Israeli war objectives: Benjamin Netanyahu seeks regime change, while Donald Trump seeks a deal that restricts Iran’s nuclear activities and guarantees shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Israeli military officials warn that a short US-led campaign could leave Israel with an even more dangerous Iran.
According to the report:
🔶 IDF doubts several days of airstrikes could bring down the Iranian government or permanently cripple its nuclear and missile capabilities
🔶 Iran increasingly sees the acquisition of nuclear weapons as essential to its survival and deterrence, and has improved protection around sensitive facilities
🔶 military strikes might delay its nuclear program, but stopping it would likely require a diplomatic deal backed by international inspections
🔶 despite economic damage and mounting pressure, Israeli assessments suggest the Iranian government could survive for at least another two years, outlasting Trump's presidency
🔶 Israel fears Iran could widen the conflict by targeting undersea communications cables, Gulf technology infrastructure or even opening a ground front in the region
The prospect of renewed fighting looms amid stalled negotiations and a [US military buildup](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76929) in the Middle East, including a third aircraft carrier heading to the region.
